# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers are about subs not showing up and the schedule slipping being more pressing than the log, so one group named in plain site language is exactly how a super would sort them.
whys.g2: There is no junk, explicit or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk got grouped.

founder.order_why: It runs from who and where, to the window, to the problem card, to how common and how often, then other difficulties and today's workaround, which is the order I'd explain my own business in.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same kicker and question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.'); if 5 is only a review of 3 it is fine, but it reads as being asked twice.
founder.missing: Nothing asks who pays. In my business the superintendent uses Fresco but the general contractor buys it, per site per month, so the study should separate user from buyer. Nothing asks about the solution (narrated walk videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC) or the price (about $1k per site per month), though this may be a problem-only flow. Screen 4 also has typos ('photoss', 'dailyy').

PRIMARY.order_why: It asks what I'd most like made easier before asking how the log actually went, so I'm picking a fix before I've walked back through the evening; and screens 1 and 2 both say 1 of 4.
PRIMARY.missing: How long it took me, especially getting the day's photos off my phone and uploaded into Procore, which is the part that eats a few hours; also whether the log ended up needed as a record, like backing up a delay dispute with the owner, which is why I bother keeping it accurate. And it assumes I typed it in the trailer when some nights it's in the truck or at home.

screens.why7: All five rungs are on the one time measure, best to worst, with a working first rung above the line and 'never got written up that day' as outright failure; the bar names the exact first rung, the balance is one against and four for so the belief can be supported or refuted, and the escape belongs on the stranger's item rather than this Check.
screens.instead: Keep it, but make rung 4 its own step on the clock: Typed up within half an hour of the walk · Took about an hour in the trailer · Took a couple of hours after the walk · Took three hours or more, into the evening · Never got written up that day

screens.why1: Saving my answers and setting up the interviewer is the obvious step before strangers see the study, right after I checked what Keel wrote about the problem.
screens.why2: "Save your answers" is plain, but "lock and record the face Keel preselects" made me read it twice to work out that "face" means the AI interviewer's on-screen look, not something about my job sites.
screens.why3: It asks me about my own study and how it will be shown, which is mine to decide.
screens.why4: Accepting Keel's preselected interviewer is a fair default, but the label doesn't say what the other choices are or that I can change the face before locking it.
screens.why5: Nothing here rewrites my superintendents, the daily log or Fresco's mechanism; it only saves what I already confirmed.
screens.instead: Save your answers -- options: "Save and use the interviewer Keel picked" / "Pick a different interviewer before saving"

screens.why1: Choosing how superintendents will take the study is the natural last step after saving my answers and before a link goes out.
screens.why2: The options are plain, but the heading 'New link' doesn't say what I'm choosing, so I need a second look at the options to see it's asking how my supers will answer.
screens.why3: I know my supers: on their phones, often in the trailer or on a loud site, so I can judge whether reading and tapping or a talking AI face suits them.
screens.why4: Read and tap, an AI interviewer, or letting them choose covers the ways it could go, the three don't overlap, and no escape is needed for a setup choice.
screens.why5: Nothing I typed is restated here, so nothing has drifted, and no product or role name leaks into what a respondent would see.
screens.instead: How should superintendents answer when they open your link? -- Read and tap / AI interviewer asks aloud / Let them choose

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside 'Frequency: 4 counted', but the line singles out Frequency when three cards are short, and leaves the '5 needed' that makes 4 decisive down on the card.
screens.why_b2: The tally '1 holding · 3 too few to call · 7 people answered' reads at once, but the kicker's '4 TO 7 COUNTED' and Prevalence's 'bar 6 of 7' (my 8 in 10 turned into a count) need a second look.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence and Frequency are my beliefs, but Importance is a clumsy 'five things that are hard' sentence, and Current solution has become 'still falls short' rather than my end-of-day hours in the trailer.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: not that one or two more counted supers would settle three of the four beliefs, and not whether the problem stage is safe to build on.
screens.why_b5: Low n is said plainly and 6 of 7 is only 'Holding up', but my own pitch ('spend hours a day', 'most of it is for liability') sits unlabelled under the verdict, where it reads like a finding from these seven.
screens.instead: Too few to call: Prevalence holds (6 of 7 typed up a log this week), but Frequency, Importance and Current solution each counted 4 of the 5 needed; get one or two more superintendents to answer before reading the problem as held or not.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Holding up' sits right beside its deciding number, '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I know it held and by exactly how much.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against over 7 people, with my bar marked at 6 on a 0 to 7 axis, so what's counted, over how many, and where the bar sits read at first look.
screens.why_b3: It's recognisably my belief and my gate question, but the card drops 'on commercial jobs' from the people I named, and the tail '— the most recent time it happened' doesn't fit a yes/no question about the last 5 working days.
screens.why_b4: 'Common among these 7, at your bar exactly' plus a pointer to the next two cards tells me where to look next, but not what this means for Fresco, such as that the pain is widespread but one more No would have sunk it.
screens.why_b5: n=7 stays visible, the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and 'at your bar exactly' keeps 'Holding up' from reading as strong.
screens.instead: At least 8 in 10 construction superintendents on commercial jobs typed up the daily log after site walks: 6 of 7 said yes, exactly my bar, so one more No would have put it below. It's common, but this small group can't settle it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right on top of '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know why it isn't called and which number decides it.
screens.why_b2: I can see that four supers were counted and the middle answer was 5 of 5, but the bar reads '4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3)' with only four cells filled, the axis starts at a 0 nobody could pick, and 'short of it' is in the legend when nobody fell short, so it takes me a second look.
screens.why_b3: 'Type up the daily log after site walks on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' is my window and my range, in the words my supers use for the end-of-day log.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that all four counted were inside my range, so one more superintendent's answer would likely settle it.
screens.why_b5: n is visible (6 answered, 4 counted, Hank and Luis named with the reason each was left out) and the small group is called a lean, not a call, which nothing contradicts; the stray 'the most recent time it happened' tag and Hank's doubled 'would rather not say' are clutter, not overclaims.
screens.instead: Too few to call: all 4 counted said 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days, inside your range, and one more counted answer would decide it, so get one more superintendent to answer before you lean on how often this happens.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know it isn't decided and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The chart says plainly it counts 8 picks from 4 people, and the bars add up, but the bar reads 'your bar · 4 of 5' right next to '4 counted', so it took me a second look to see that 4 of 5 is the number needed for me, not the count.
screens.why_b3: Importance, and 'Typing up the daily log after the site walks' as one of the two they'd most like made easier among five things after the walks, is my belief in my words.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' tells me not to act, but not what to do, such as get one more superintendent counted, and it ignores that both people against picked the schedule and the subs over the log.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, who was left out and why) and the small group is named as not a call, though 'a lean' is a stretch on a 2-2 split.
screens.instead: 2 of 4 put the log in their two and the 2 against both picked the schedule and the subs; you need 4 of 5 for it to hold, so get at least one more superintendent counted before you lean on the log being what hurts most.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside "4 counted · 5 needed to call it", so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The rungs, the counts and my line read at a glance, but the strip's "your bar · 4 of 5" with the marker at 4, when only 4 were counted and 3 count for me, took me a second look to see that it means the bar as it would stand at five people.
screens.why_b3: It is my belief and my time measure, but it says "most construction superintendents" without "on commercial jobs", and "typing the daily log in the trailer" is Keel's phrase for what I called uploading photos and creating the log at the end of the day.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" is generic: it doesn't say that one more answer settles it, or that the 3 of 4 lean toward my belief.
screens.why_b5: n is shown, both people left out are named with the reason, and "a small group: a lean, not a call" keeps it from being read as held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted took an hour or more after the walk, a lean toward 'falls short'; one more answer decides it, so don't read it as held yet.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief line are mine: the daily log after the site walks as one of the two things a superintendent would most like made easier.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed' implies I need one more counted answer, but the screen never says that schedule and subs beating the log is a warning for an idea sold on the log, or what to ask next.
screens.why_b5: The n stays visible (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked), it is called too few, and no theme is claimed beyond the two people who said it.
screens.why_b6: I learn that the log loses to schedule and subs, and that one super finishes the log on the tablet before the gate while another lets it wait till morning; neither is in what I typed.
screens.instead: Too few to call (4 of 5): both who put the log below other work picked schedule and subs; Denise already finishes it on site and Ray lets it slip to morning, so ask whether Fresco can sell on the walk's follow-ups, not on the log.

screens.why1: It's the first thing to settle before asking me anything about my daily logs: whether my jobs are on Procore or ACC at all, so it's obvious why it opens the study.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are what every super I know says out loud, and I'd answer this on first hearing even though 'jobs you're running now run on' doubles up the word a bit.
screens.why3: I know exactly which platform each of my current jobs is on, since the GC sets it and I'm in it every day.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a screener, and any one job on either platform makes it a yes, so there's no missing answer.
screens.why5: Procore and ACC are my trade's words, not the founder's, and nothing of their product shows through.
screens.why6: One short question and two options; ACC is said as letters that supers use out loud anyway, so it travels fine.
screens.instead: Are any of your current jobs on Procore or ACC? Yes or No.

screens.why1: Right after confirming my jobs run on Procore, asking whether I typed up the daily log this week is the obvious next thing to ask a super.
screens.why2: "Type up the daily log after site walks" is exactly how I'd say it; I can answer on first hearing, though "your site walks" would read a touch smoother.
screens.why3: It's my own last week of logs, so I know whether I sat in the trailer typing it up or got it done on the walk.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and my true answer is there either way; the chips beside it belong to the story box, not the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing about any product or the founder's plan comes through; it's just my daily log in my own words.
screens.why6: One short sentence then "Yes or no" is easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: The gate asks the founder's problem as one act in the window, not the routine of logging photos and notes, so a super who finished the log on the walk can truly say No and one who typed it up afterwards says Yes, with no escape as the card requires.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: I just said yes to typing up the daily log this week, so asking how many of those five days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, site walks and working days are all words I use every day; I'd say 'fill out the daily' more than 'type up', but I get it on first read.
screens.why3: I know exactly which days this week I did the log myself after walking the job, so I can answer without guessing.
screens.why4: One button per day from 1 to 5 covers every true answer for someone who already said yes, none overlap, and 'I can't recall' fits as the out.
screens.why5: It asks about my own daily log and nothing about any product or app leaks through; it reads like my own week.
screens.why6: One short question, then 'a number from 1 to 5' and the escape; I can hear it once and say 'five'.
screens.why7: Every option counts working days of the 5-day window, 1 first and 5 last, with no 0 and no bands, and 'I can't recall' sits apart; a founder low of 2 or more leaves buttons on both sides of the belief.

screens.why1: After asking whether and how often I typed up the log, it makes sense to ask how that stacks up against the other end-of-day stuff I've got to get through after the walk.
screens.why2: Subs, RFIs, the schedule, the daily log and the walk are all words I use every day, so I'd answer this on first read.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I do myself after walking the site, so I know which ones eat my evening.
screens.why4: Five distinct things a super deals with after the walk, nothing silly or doubled up, and None of these fits if none of them bugs me.
screens.why5: Nothing here hints at any product or app; it just lists my own work in words I'd use.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options read as a list I can hold, then one escape, easy to answer by ear.
screens.why7: The own row, typing up the log after the walk, is there and not first, with four rivals from the same moment and None of these at the first ask, so picks can land for or against.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? (same five options, None of these)

screens.why1: Right after asking which part of my last daily log I'd want made easier, asking how the typing actually went is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Typing the daily log in the trailer after the walk is exactly how I'd say it, so I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I do this every working day and I know roughly how long last night's log took me.
screens.why4: The options mix two things: the first rung says how soon after the walk it was done, the others say how long it took. 'A couple of hours' and 'the rest of the evening' can both be true of the same night. The stem's 'in the trailer' doesn't fit the nights I finish it on the tablet in the truck or at home.
screens.why5: Nothing of any product or company comes through; it's just my daily log and my trailer.
screens.why6: One short question and five short options I can hold, then one escape, which says cleanly aloud.
screens.why7: The ladder works: it has working rungs at the top and a last rung where it fails outright, so the belief can go either way. Two rules bend. Rung one grades how soon after the walk rather than how long the typing took, so not every rung is on one time measure. And the escape is 'I can't recall' where the card wants 'Someone else did it', since a log can be handed to a field engineer.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did typing it up take? Under half an hour; about an hour; a couple of hours; most of the evening; or it didn't get done that day. Or say someone else typed it up.
